language_instructions: For English (eng) social-media text, focus on explicit emotion words (e.g., 'love', 'hate', 'sad', 'wow'), intensifiers ('really', 'so', 'absolutely'), punctuation ('!', '?', '!?'), capitalisation ('AMAZING'), emojis (e.g., 😊 joy, 😡 anger, 😲 surprise, 😢 sadness, 🤢 disgust, 😱 fear), sarcasm cues ('yeah right', '/s'), and context (e.g., Reddit threads, replies, quote-replies).

reasoning_examples.text: I can't believe you would do something so stupid.

reasoning.interpretations: First, the insult and frustration signal anger; second, could be disappointment but the directed insult dominates
reasoning.critique: Matches a typical English rebuke; best fit is anger. Conclusion: anger

reasoning.interpretations: First, 'OMG' signals surprise; second, 'got the job' and 🎉 evoke joy
reasoning.critique: Matches an announcement post; best fit is joy and surprise. Conclusion: joy, surprise

reasoning_examples.text: Pineapple on pizza is absolutely revolting 🤢

reasoning.interpretations: First, 'revolting' and 🤢 signal disgust; second, could be mild anger but no target person
reasoning.critique: Standard food-opinion disgust trope; best fit is disgust. Conclusion: disgust

reasoning_examples.text: Wait what?? They cancelled the show? I'm devastated and honestly terrified what's next

reasoning.interpretations: First, double-question signals surprise; second, 'devastated' evokes sadness; third, 'terrified' evokes fear
reasoning.critique: Multi-label fits a cascading reaction; best fit is fear, sadness, surprise. Conclusion: fear, sadness, surprise

reasoning_examples.text: I think the meeting is at 3 pm tomorrow.

reasoning.cues: no emotion words, no emoji, no intensifier
reasoning.interpretations: First, a statement of plans; second, no compelling cue for any of the 6 categories
reasoning.critique: Default to all-zeros when there is no compelling evidence. Conclusion: none
